elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 is omitted, and Section 12.3 expressly states that Customer has made no non-compete commitment and may develop, acquire, license, sell, or use any product or service.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains, so no unnamed or broadly defined competing product is restricted.

elements.element: Any restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains during or after the term; the former 24-month post-term restriction is omitted.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains, so its duration cannot exceed 12 months.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 affirmatively permits Customer to develop any product or service without restriction.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 affirmatively permits Customer to acquire any product or service without restriction.

result.reason: The operative redline fully achieves the preferred position by deleting the non-compete and retaining Section 12.3's express protection against non-compete and field-of-use restrictions. It therefore also satisfies the fallback limitations because no restriction exists to exceed them. The change is limited to omission of the conflicting Section 12.4 and does not alter unrelated commercial terms.
